_source: JPL DSN Telecommunications Link Design Handbook 810-005: module 301 rev N (station coordinates, Table 5; generic elevation limits, sec. 2.2.2), module 104 rev L (34-m BWG, Tables 3 and 7), module 101 rev H (70-m, Tables 1, 2 and 4), module 105 rev E (atmosphere, eqs. 1 and 2, Tables 13 to 18), module 106 rev B (solar corona, eq. 7 and sec. 2.3). Public documents, https://deepspace.jpl.nasa.gov/dsndocs/810-005/
_complexes_note: WGS 84 geodetic coordinates of DSS 24 (Goldstone), DSS 34 (Canberra) and DSS 54 (Madrid), 301 Table 5, rounded to 1e-5 deg (about 1 m).
_antennas_note: 34m X: DSS-34 X/Ka feed (104 Table 7: 68.32 dBi, TAMW 16.28 K RCP; Table 3: 67.03 dBi transmit, 20 kW, 0.6 dB waveguide). 70m X: DSS-43 S/X mode (101 Table 2: 74.36 dBi, Table 4: TAMW 13.32 K; DSS-14 12.59 K used as the three-station value) and Table 1 (73.23 dBi transmit, 20 kW). No 70-m Ka-band.
_atmosphere_note: Year-average zenith attenuation at cumulative distribution CD = 0.50 and 0.90 (105 Tables 13 to 18). Attenuation at elevation theta is Azen / sin(theta) (eq. 2); its noise is TM (1 - 10^(-A/10)) with TM = 255 + 25 CD kelvin (eq. 1); the cosmic background (2.725 K) is attenuated by the same factor.

solar_corona._note: Scintillation index m(theta) = min(1, exp(-a1 d + a2 + a3 d + a4 d^2)) with d = theta - theta_t, from 106 eq. 7 (m = 1 below theta_t). The printed equation lost its minus sign in the PDF text; it is read as a decay because Figures 5 and 6 show m falling with SEP angle. It is a reported diagnostic only: contact rules use the section 2.3 limits below. Section 2.3: X-band data return works down to at least 2.3 deg SEP, Ka-band down to 1 deg. The command moratorium below 2 deg is NASA's Mars practice (for example the 2019, 2021 and 2023 Mars solar conjunctions: no commands sent while Mars is within about 2 deg of the Sun as seen from Earth).
